chalisa.do1: Victory to you, daughter of the mountain, daughter of Dakṣa, beloved of Śiva, mine of virtues, mother of Gaṇapati, Pārvatī, Ambā, Śakti, Bhavānī.
chalisa.cau1: Brahmā cannot find your secret; the five-faced Śiva meditates on you always. ॥1॥
chalisa.cau2: The six-faced Kārttikeya cannot tell your glory; the thousand-mouthed Śeṣa labours hard at it. ॥2॥
chalisa.cau3: Even they, Mother, who stand in their places ordering protection and dissolution, do not reach your end. ॥3॥
chalisa.cau4: Your lips are red like coral; your eyes, darkened with kohl, are most lovely. ॥4॥
chalisa.cau5: Your graceful forehead is anointed with saffron, and the beauty of the kumkum and the grains of rice upon it captivates the mind. ॥5॥
chalisa.cau6: You are adorned with golden garments and a bodice; a divine girdle sways at your waist. ॥6॥
chalisa.cau7: A garland of madār flowers graces your throat; seeing it, the mind is charmed at once. ॥7॥
chalisa.cau8: You bear the endless beauty of the rising sun's glow; the beauty of your ornaments is lovely. ॥8॥
chalisa.cau9: There is a throne studded with gems of many kinds, on which Viṣṇu and the four-faced Brahmā shine. ॥9॥
chalisa.cau10: You are worshipped by your retinue, Indra and the rest, and around you resound the cries of the world's beasts, nāgas and yakṣas. ॥10॥
chalisa.cau11: Dweller on Mount Kailāsa, victory, victory to you; you who spread a radiance of millions, victory, victory to you. ॥11॥
chalisa.cau12: All the three worlds are your family; your light is in every atom. ॥12॥
chalisa.cau13: Maheśa is the lord of your life, he who ever guards the three worlds. ॥13॥
chalisa.cau14: When you won a husband such as he, your merits of old came to light. ॥14॥
chalisa.cau15: He whose mount is an old bull: who can sing his glory? ॥15॥
chalisa.cau16: Śiva ever roams the cremation grounds; fearsome serpents are his ornaments. ॥16॥
chalisa.cau17: The hue of the hālāhala poison spread over his throat, and he won the title of Nīlakaṇṭha, the blue-throated. ॥17॥
chalisa.cau18: He did this to make the gods glad: taking the poison himself, he gave them nectar. ॥18॥
chalisa.cau19: You are his wife, beautiful in form, destroyer of sin, bringer of good. ॥19॥
chalisa.cau20: Seeing your supreme beauty, which fills the three worlds with wonder, ॥20॥
chalisa.cau21: Mother Gaṅgā grew afraid; the waves of her water are full of shame. ॥21॥
chalisa.cau22: Like a co-wife she came to Śiva; leaving Viṣṇu's lotus feet, she rushed to him. ॥22॥
chalisa.cau23: Her lotus face withered; seeing this, Śiva swiftly set her upon his head. ॥23॥
chalisa.cau24: You give everlasting bliss and grant boons; you make your devotees fearless and never leave them. ॥24॥
chalisa.cau25: You destroy all sins and the three afflictions, Māheśvarī, daughter of the Himālaya. ॥25॥
chalisa.cau26: The city of Kāśī was ever dear to your heart, and you made it a siddha-pīṭha, a seat of spiritual power. ॥26॥
chalisa.cau27: Bhagavatī, you give alms every day, and bestow grace, delight and love. ॥27॥
chalisa.cau28: Destroyer of enemies, victory, victory to you, Ambā; you, our refuge, make speech come true. ॥28॥
chalisa.cau29: You are Gaurī, Umā, Śaṅkarī, Kālī, and Annapūrṇā, who nourishes the world. ॥29॥
chalisa.cau30: You are Bhagavatī, sovereign of all people; Satī, whose life is her husband, the supreme Goddess. ॥30॥
chalisa.cau31: You performed hard austerities when you had taken instruction from Nārada. ॥31॥
chalisa.cau32: Neither food nor water nor air was your sustenance; your body became nothing but bones. ॥32॥
chalisa.cau33: Even leaves and grass did not please you as food; then you gained the name Umā. ॥33॥
chalisa.cau34: Seeing your penance, the seven sages came; they tried to shake you, but you did not waver, and they were defeated. ॥34॥
chalisa.cau35: Then they hailed you: Victory, victory, victory; and the seven sages went back to their own homes. ॥35॥
chalisa.cau36: Then the gods, Brahmā and Viṣṇu came to you and spoke of granting you a boon. ॥36॥
chalisa.cau37: Umā, you asked them for a husband as your boon: him from whom the world seeks the treasure of the three worlds. ॥37॥
chalisa.cau38: The two said: So be it, and went away; you had the fruit of your wish. ॥38॥
chalisa.cau39: Having married Śiva, fair lady, you were once more called the wife of Hara. ॥39॥
chalisa.cau40: Whoever reads this Chālīsā, the Lord will give him wealth, family and happiness. ॥40॥
chalisa.do2: You whose fair head is crowned with moonlight, mine of happiness, victory, victory to you. Pārvatī, for the good of your devotees, remain ever the giver of boons.
